messages:
anna: FYI I'm hitting a gap with the Python SDK and OpenTelemetry. AsyncClient calls don't carry trace headers so our traces stop at the Redwood call.

ben: Do you have a tiny repro? async or sync? which HTTP backend?

anna: async + httpx backend. Minimal: 
```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
from opentelemetry import trace
client = AsyncClient(api_key='...')
tracer = trace.get_tracer(__name__)
async with tracer.start_as_current_span('test'):
    await client.chat.complete('hello')
```
No traceparent header on egress.

claire: I inspected client/_transport.py — headers are composed there and it falls back to env vars for request id. It never calls propagators.inject. Sync path that uses requests gets instrumented by requests-instrumentation, so this is an async parity bug.

diego: Two practical fixes: (1) optional OTEL integration that calls propagators.inject when opentelemetry is installed, (2) a middleware hook so users can add headers like x-redwood-request-id or tenant.

ben: Middleware shape idea: add_middleware(fn) where fn receives (req, next) and can be sync or async. We'll need typing Protocols for MiddlewareSync and MiddlewareAsync so mypy users aren't broken.

anna: Also typing: streaming responses currently have poor stubs (Any). We should change to AsyncIterator[str] or AsyncIterator[Token] and add TypedDicts for Request/Response shapes so middleware gets typed. MyPy is failing across repos because of this.

claire: Small UX detail: don't import opentelemetry at top-level. Make integration optional via extras like redwood[tracing]. If not installed, no-op. Preserve user-provided request-id header; only generate uuid4 when missing. Use header name x-redwood-request-id (lowercase internally).

diego: Tests: stub httpx transport to capture outgoing headers and use opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export.InMemorySpanExporter to assert traceparent was injected. Add both sync+async tests.

anna: Interim workaround for users: manually inject headers and pass extra_headers: 
```py
from opentelemetry.propagators.textmap import inject
headers = {}
inject(headers)
await client.chat.complete('hi', extra_headers=headers)
```
Document this in migration notes.

ben: Proposed client options: Client(..., propagate_tracing=False) default false for now, Client.add_middleware(fn), built-in RequestIdMiddleware. Document middleware order as FIFO.

ci-bot: CI queued for branch async-otel-fix (PR #501).

claire: I'll open an RFC for middleware typing and include examples (FastAPI dependency attaching request-id, example OTLP collector config).

anna: Thanks everyone. If someone wants to pair on the async test tomorrow morning ping me. :+1:
